public_context.instructions: Select one RISC-V custom instruction, or the unchanged baseline. Maximize VERIFIED FEASIBLE whole-program speedup within the measurement-attempt budget. Predictions are uncalibrated, not measurements. Consider all provided heuristics, structure, uncertainty, area, timing and measurement cost. Use only list_candidates, predict, measure and finalize. Every submitted measure request, including an invalid ID or repeat, consumes an attempt; failed measurements also count. No unqueried outcome is available. Only the current incumbent may be finalized: use incumbent.candidate_id exactly, or use null only when incumbent.candidate_id is null. The host computes the best paid, correct, device-fitting, area/timing-feasible improvement; never finalize a stale, unmeasured, infeasible, or lower-speedup candidate. Check remaining.decision_turns_after_this_response and provider_calls_available_including_this_response. Each provider response permits one tool action; reserve a later call to finalize after a measurement. If the remaining decision/provider allowance is exhausted, the host selects its verified incumbent or baseline. You may stop early. Every measure action must include a concise public-evidence decision_summary of at most 320 characters. Do not provide private chain of thought. The final summary you submit is an unverified agent note; the host returns the authoritative measured result. Single instructions only; individual speedups and area cannot be added. This is a prospective live hardware-measurement session on a new workload group. The target source and exact operator-tree families are excluded from training; this is one fixed Sudoku instance and does not establish broad workload generalization. Each measure action triggers one real, one-attempt target evaluation. The request may include current_grouped_ml_bundle metadata. When present, the predict tool returns pairwise_rank_score (an ordering score, not a speedup estimate), pairwise_rank_position, factorized_feasibility_probability and factorized_decision_score for the 64-LUT4 cap. Feasibility scores and their ensemble disagreement are uncalibrated; disagreement is not a confidence interval. A selection_board appears after predict and separates the frozen pairwise order, analytic latency estimate, uncalibrated feasibility-like signals and paid verification. Its advisory default is the highest-ranked unattempted candidate; it is not mandatory. If you override it, explain the public evidence in decision_summary. Never infer area or feasibility from operation count or the uncalibrated score. The decision score is feasibility score multiplied by the nonnegative public analytic cycle-reduction estimate. Only a paid outcome verifies area, timing and correctness.

actual_dataset_collection.scope: full-pool corpus/oracle collection; costs all twelve measured attempts, irrespective of replay budget

policy_costs_note: Each non-agent policy is replayed with one-at-a-time outcome release and counts only its own B1/B2/B3 prefix. Those are offline counterfactual decision costs on already collected target labels; actual corpus construction measured the complete pool.

prior_relay_startup_failure.attempt: r2 non-PTY Codex chat bridge launch
prior_relay_startup_failure.launch_mode: exec_command without a PTY; recorded from the invocation used for this attempt
prior_relay_startup_failure.cause: The stdin-driven bridge returned CodexChatBridgeError before a usable action. The saved ledger preserves only the exception class, not its message; EOF is the likely cause inferred from the non-PTY invocation, not independently verifiable.
prior_relay_startup_failure.disposition: Preserved unchanged. Do not score this as an agent selection; retry only in a new source-bound preregistration with an enforced live PTY.

source_family_audit.family_definition: Canonical operator-tree shape that ignores constants and input identities and sorts children for commutative add/and/or/xor/mul nodes.
source_family_audit.interpretation: Target source and every canonical operator-tree family in the target pool are excluded from training. This is one held-out workload and remains too small for a broad generalization claim.

limitations: One agent episode is exploratory and has no model-family or agent-superiority power.
Current Codex model ID, provider tokens, and isolated inference latency are unavailable.
The current relay is cooperative, not an isolated tool sandbox.
One fixed Sudoku puzzle; no arbitrary-puzzle generalization.
Single-instruction pool; no combined instruction labels.
One held-out workload does not establish broad generalization.
Pool is the top-12 executable shortlist from the existing merit-oriented extractor, not all legal instructions.
Historical model-selection decisions are development evidence; this run tests zero-shot transfer on a held-out workload.
The measured oracle is complete only if all twelve attempts produce classifiable outcomes.
FPGA synthesis/routing and RTL simulation are not silicon measurements.
Single-instruction measurements do not establish combined-instruction performance.
One fixed Sudoku source and puzzle are not sufficient to establish broad workload generalization; exact operation-tree-family holdout is also a stricter, narrower transfer test.
The LLM result is one current-chat relay episode without an available deployment ID, provider tokens or isolated API execution.
Five ML seeds are dependent algorithm runs on one candidate pool, not independent workload replicates.
An unresolved or infrastructure-censored outcome makes exhaustive-oracle speedup and regret unavailable; conclusively incorrect candidates are disqualified as infeasible.
This study evaluates individual instructions; it does not test combined instruction sets or full processor implementation of selected combinations.
